related_questions.question: What stage is prostate cancer with bone metastases?
related_questions.snippet: Patients with cancer locally confined to the pelvis, but involving adjacent organs or lymph nodes have localized stage IV or D1 prostate cancer. Patients with disease that has spread to distant organs, most commonly the spine, ribs, pelvis and other bones have metastatic stage IV or D2 prostate cancer.
related_questions.title: Stage IV (D) Prostate Cancer - Texas Oncology

related_questions.question: What is bone metastasis in prostate cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Bone metastasis is when cancer spreads to your bones from another part of your body. It often affects people with breast, lung and prostate cancer. Bone pain is the most common symptom, but bone fracture also often happens. Bone metastasis typically affects your spine, but can also affect arms and legs.
related_questions.title: Bone Metastasis (Cancer Spread to Bone) - Cleveland Clinic

related_questions.question: What would you call prostate cancer that has spread to the bones?
related_questions.snippet: Metastatic prostate cancer means the cancer has spread from the prostate to other parts of the body. It is sometimes called advanced prostate cancer. It most commonly spreads to lymph nodes in other parts of the body or to the bones.

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10 codes for prostate cancer with bone metastasis are:

list.snippet: C79.51: Secondary malignant neoplasm of bone
C61: This code represents the primary site of the cancer, which is the prostate.
C79.51: This code indicates that the cancer has metastasized (spread) to the bone.

text_blocks.snippet: If a patient has prostate cancer that has spread to the femur, the ICD-10 codes would be C61 and C79.51.

list.snippet: Additional codes may be necessary to specify the exact location and type of bone metastasis.
